subject: Post-demo alignment: retention windows, resident zones, and break-glass procedures
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@harborbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick recap & follow-ups on data handling

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our demo and the items we agreed to follow up on:

- Data residency: Harbor Bank asked about multi-region pinning (US-only) and export controls.
- PII retention windows: what retention tiers we can enforce at route/tenant level.
- Support access: least-privilege support roles, break-glass process, and audit trail retention.
- Logging: what telemetry/logs we expose and for how long (tokens redacted).

Next steps we committed to: 1) provide a short table of retention options + recommended defaults, 2) draft a short runbook for support break-glass with SLA and approval flow, 3) confirm SOC2 scope and evidence we can share.

Attaching a high-level SOC2 snapshot and a sample retention table (draft). Marcus

[Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf, 240KB)]
[Attachment: retention-table.csv (csv, 12KB)]

From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@harborbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia.park@harborbank.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap & follow-ups on data handling

Thanks Marcus — useful recap. A few clarifying Qs from our security team: 

1) Residency: we need guarantees that data for our prod tenants will not leave US regions; is that configurable per-customer? Is there a default multi-az vs multi-region tradeoff?

2) Retention: can you support a 30/180/1095 day model by data class (PII/PHI/derived embeddings)? We need a CSV we can import into our data policy tooling.

3) Break-glass: our ops team wants a two-person approval for emergency decryption/access and a full audit trail (who, why, when). Can Redwood integrate the approval step with our ticketing system (Jira)?

Please loop in anyone internal who should respond. If possible, can we get the runbook draft by end of week?

Tom

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@harborbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap & follow-ups on data handling

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. I run security for Customer Success engagement on controls; below are concrete answers and a proposed path forward.

Residency
- Yes: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning. For Harbor Bank we can enforce US-only residency at the tenant level; workloads run in a chosen region set (e.g., us-west-2 + us-east-1) for HA.
- Tradeoff: multi-az within a single region minimizes cross-region transfer vs multi-region for added RPO/RTO. We'll recommend multi-az within a single US region unless you need cross-region failover.

Retention
- We support retention policies scoped by data class. Sample tiers we propose (we will deliver as CSV you can import):
  - PII (raw): 30 days
  - PII (derived/embeddings): 180 days
  - Non-PII logs/telemetry: 90 days
  - Audit logs: 3650 days (10 years) — configurable per contract
- We can automate deletion hooks and provide deletion proof records (timestamp + object id) for audits.

Support access & break-glass
- Least-privilege model: support engineers get role-scoped tokens that only allow troubleshooting APIs; no direct access to raw customer payloads unless elevated.
- Break-glass: we implement a time-bound elevation that requires: 1) a ticket id, 2) two approvers (one from customer and one from Redwood security or CS manager), 3) automatic audit log and snapshot saved to the tenant's audit object store. Access window is configurable (default 30 minutes).
- Integration: we have a webhook pattern and Jira integration templates that can tie the approval step to a Jira transition (we'll share the template).

Attachments: I attached a draft runbook for break-glass and the retention CSV. I've also included a short SOC2 evidence index to indicate what we can share under an NDA.

Action items we propose:
- I will send the import-ready retention CSV by EOD Wednesday.
- Grace: can you coordinate the draft customer approval SLA language (two-person approval and Jira workflow) for legal signoff?

Evelyn

[Attachment: support-access-runbook.md (md, 9KB)]
[Attachment: retention-table.csv (csv, 12KB)]
[Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf, 240KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@harborbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap & follow-ups on data handling

Tom — looping back with the SLA language draft attached and a short note on the approval flow. Highlights:

- Customer approver + Redwood security approver required for any break-glass elevation. We will record ticket id and a short reason.
- Elevation is time boxed (default 30 minutes) and auto-revoked; extended windows require re-approval.
- We can integrate with Jira by listening for a specific transition ("Approve Breakglass") and trigger the elevation via our admin API.

I've attached the suggested SLA paragraph and a sample Jira webhook payload for your security team to test. If that looks good, Marcus and I can set up a short test run (15 min) with your ops next week.

[Attachment: support-sla-draft.docx (docx, 6KB)]

Thanks,
Grace

From: Tom Reynolds <t.reynolds@harborbank.com>

Grace — this is exactly what we needed, thanks. Two quick asks before we book the test session:

1) Can you include a sample audit record (redacted) that shows how the proof-of-deletion and break-glass audit will look?
2) For the retention CSV, can you include an explicit mapping column for our internal policy keys so we can import cleanly?

If you can send those today, we'll target a 30-minute test with ops next Tue (12 Aug).

Tom
